rules.TESTED: needs >=1 existing test; no UI is implied
rules.INTEGRATED: needs tests AND a working UI AND enforced authorization and audit end to end
rules.DESIGNED: design or partial building blocks only

capabilities.done: RFM behavioural segmentation over the synthetic order history, persisted as tenant segments with evidence basis and size-based confidence; an assumption-labelled ICP segment.
capabilities.missing: No firmographic/demographic ICP modelling, no profitability-per-segment model, no UI.

capabilities.done: A research-findings store with source kind, URL, retrieval date, confidence and a mandatory limitation (search results are leads, not facts); three supplier leads and their source pages recorded with dates.
capabilities.missing: No competitor dataset, no competitor comparison and no automated research; findings are entered by people or seeded.

capabilities.done: Unit-economics primitives plus a stored-data financial model: gross and contribution margin, fixed costs, break-even, payback, price sensitivity and scenario comparison, shown in the Financial Plan. Milestone 4 adds start-up cost categories, working capital, contingency, a break-even grid over price and cost changes, and formulas with the stored numbers substituted; every expected number was worked by hand before the code was run.
capabilities.missing: No niche scoring model, no CAC/LTV model, no market-size claims; scenarios describe one project, they do not rank niches.
Local preview from structured data not built; publishing must stay a separate, explicitly authorised mechanism.

capabilities.done: Margin, discount break-even, bundles, inflation, break-even units, assumption-labelled elasticity grid and revenue scenarios; NASHA costs from the existing recipe-costing module; versioned prices per tenant. Milestone 4: a supplier price effect (cheapest valid quote against the next cheapest, labelled as an illustration when prices are synthetic).
capabilities.missing: No UI; no measured willingness to pay (elasticity is an assumption).

capabilities.done: Offer table with its economics computed from stored prices and unit costs through the pricing engine (margin before and after, volume uplift needed to hold profit), shown on the Offers and campaigns screen; campaign drafts linked to an offer and audience.
capabilities.missing: Offers are seeded drafts: no create/edit screen, no approval flow, no redemption tracking, nothing is published.

capabilities.done: Lead table with source; creation audited.
capabilities.missing: No attribution model, no campaign-to-lead linkage, no workflow.

capabilities.done: Rule-based lead qualification (hand-computed oracle), run through the governed workflow: evidence-backed recommendation, source/consent/suppression validation, THE WEIR hold, human approval, audited CRM update.
capabilities.missing: No prospect discovery by design (no scraping); the score is an unvalidated rule set, not a learned model; synthetic leads only.
Needs the governed approval workflow (THE WEIR) and a proposal entity.
No drafting model or templates; no fabricated customer claims policy check yet.

capabilities.done: Consent and suppression enforcement for email DRAFTS; no send path exists by construction.
capabilities.missing: No sequence entity, scheduling or sending (sending is intentionally not implemented).

capabilities.done: content_items table with draft/in_review/approved/rejected states and a claims_checked flag.
capabilities.missing: No generation, no claim checker, no approval flow, no UI.

capabilities.implementation: Contact, account, opportunity and activity workflows
capabilities.done: Accounts, contacts, leads, opportunities, activities; DB-enforced stage rules; audited, versioned writes; role policy; RLS tenant isolation; HTTP API; web screens (CRM, pipeline, AI workflow center); governed lead-qualification workflow whose only CRM write passes THE WEIR and a human approval; mutation-tested.
capabilities.missing: No reminders, scheduled triggers or event-driven automation; synthetic data only; local demo, not a deployed service.

capabilities.done: Stage pipeline with a DB-enforced transition graph and append-only transition log, a Sales Pipeline screen whose moves are validated by the backend.
capabilities.missing: No funnel analytics or pipeline forecast.

capabilities.implementation: Creative asset management and generation workflows
capabilities.missing: No spend or generation is authorised; Runway remains unpurchased.
Needs the workflow registry (see 25).

capabilities.implementation: Sales knowledge base and objection-response assistance
capabilities.missing: Would reuse the existing status-aware retrieval stack.

capabilities.done: RFM segments include at-risk and lapsed groups.
capabilities.missing: No churn model, no retention workflow; any churn score would be simulated, not validated.
The separate experimentation-toolkit repository exists but is not integrated.

capabilities.done: Growth OS Executive Dashboard whose numbers are computed from tenant data and checked against the database; plus the existing sourced NASHA operations, reliability and security dashboards (portfolio).
capabilities.missing: Narrow KPI set; no experiments or attribution; synthetic data.

capabilities.done: Two governed workflows run through THE WEIR with a human decision: lead qualification and, new, an agent-assisted procurement recommendation (research brief on the Production AI Agent Platform engine with read-only tools, independent claim verification, deterministic recommendation re-derived independently, deterministic fallback, audited recording). Both have API, interface, failure-path and mutation tests. Milestone 4: every agent or model output crosses a strict boundary (structure, grounding, number and price checks, injection and overreach refusal, read-only tool allowlist, computed uncertainty, paid providers refused without approval) with a 28-output evaluation and one mutant per rule; the approval now advances the project in the same transaction; a 12-step journey test runs over HTTP across roles.
capabilities.missing: Two hard-coded workflows, not a generic workflow registry or scheduler; the agent provider is an offline heuristic (a real model provider has still not been exercised (no local runtime, no weights, hosted providers need approval); the live-model test is skipped and reported unverified); no triggers or reminders.
